summary: ACAD is a Big-4-audited (Ernst & Young, since 2015), no-going-concern, operating-cash-positive biotech with two FDA-approved products generating $726M+ in 2023 net product sales. The -54.8% pre-cutoff drawdown is NOT a solvency or auditor-walk story. Instead, the lying-detector framework surfaces two SEVERE pre-cutoff narrative collapses: (1) the 10-K's headline 'late-stage growth' anchor — ADVANCE-2 in Q1 2024 — failed its Phase 3 primary endpoint on 2024-03-11, only 11 days after the 10-K was filed, marking ACAD's THIRD pimavanserin label-expansion setback after two prior FDA CRLs on dementia-related psychosis; and (2) DAYBUE, the launch story the 10-K describes as 'strong demand with strong persistency,' showed its FIRST sequential decline (-14% QoQ) in the Q1 2024 10-Q filed pre-cutoff, the canonical early warning that Rett-syndrome launch persistency is degrading. Two MODERATE catches: the 10-K's pimavanserin-extension batting average is poorly framed (3 setbacks across DRP/ADP/schizophrenia), and ClinicalTrials.gov shows a 24% termination rate that the pipeline narrative does not foreground. Solvency, auditor, customer-concentration disclosure, and safety overhang all PASS. The story is not corporate fraud — it is a small/mid-cap biotech where management's forward-looking growth narrative was invalidated by its own subsequent public filings INSIDE the cutoff window, a textbook claim-evolution detection.
